# Prune 7 stale local branches that block the ship Step 1 unmerged-branches gate

## Problem statement

The `ship` skill's Step 1 gate (`scripts/check-unmerged-branches.js`) lists every local branch not merged into `dev` and aborts the release (exit 3) unless `--skip-checks` is passed. Seven stale local branches from the herdr implement workflow currently fail this gate, so the TCE v0.1.17 dev→main release had to be run with `--skip-checks` (all other gates were verified manually). `git branch --no-merged dev` currently reports **eight** refs — the seven below plus the protected `worklog/data`, which the gate filters out.

These branches share an old merge-base (`567ae2d4`) and diverge from `dev` by 360–430 files. Merging them would produce hundreds of conflicts, so the desired outcome is safe local-ref removal after per-branch verification — **not** merging.

## Users

- **Release operator / producer (primary)** — needs the ship Step 1 gate to pass without `--skip-checks` so releases are trustworthy and repeatable.
  *As a release operator, I want `git branch --no-merged dev` to list no stale branches so that `ship` Step 1 passes without bypasses.*
- **Engine maintainer (secondary)** — needs confidence that no unmerged work is silently discarded.
  *As a maintainer, I want each branch triaged against `dev` so that I can see exactly which commits are already represented and which are not.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the seven branches is triaged with `git cherry dev <branch>` (patch-id); the per-branch result (represented vs unrepresented commits) is recorded.
2. Branches whose content is fully represented on `dev` are deleted (local refs); any worktree holding a checked-out branch is removed first (`git worktree remove`, then `git branch -D`).
3. Any branch carrying commits NOT represented on `dev` is surfaced to the producer with the commit SHAs and subjects **before** deletion. No unreviewed work is discarded; deletion of such branches proceeds only on explicit producer approval (or after a documented backup ref/tag is created).
4. After cleanup, `git branch --no-merged dev` lists only protected refs (`worklog/data`), and `check-unmerged-branches.js` reports no unmerged branches (ship Step 1 passes without `--skip-checks`).
5. The main checkout and remaining worktrees are left clean; no unrelated worktrees or branches are removed.
6. Findings (per-branch triage table, deletion log, producer approvals) are recorded as a comment on this item.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (Branch pruning is expected to require no documentation change; confirm and record this explicitly.)
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (Branch pruning changes no tracked source, so the practical validation proxy is `npm run build` plus `npm test -- --project unit`.)

## Existing state (intake evidence, 2026-09-26)

`git branch --no-merged dev` → 8 refs: the 7 below + protected `worklog/data`.

Patch-id triage (`git cherry dev <branch>`; `+` = commit unrepresented on `dev`, `-` = represented):

| Branch | HEAD | On origin? | Worktree? | Patch-id verdict | Representative unrepresented commits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fix-bank-hint-tutorial` | `8ffdae34` | yes | no | unrepresented | `8ffdae34` do not fire banking hint during tutorial |
| `revert-fix` | `c8499907` | no | `/tmp/wl-revert` | unrepresented | `c8499907` track scheduled-prompts.json |
| `wl-CG-0MTIILIBQ009J49F-prd-m3-scope-note-tests-build` | `f426ffd7` | no | no | unrepresented | `f426ffd7` Implementation complete |
| `wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566-add-week-year-to-mainstreetstate-random` | `f9ea09b5` | yes | no | **fully represented** | none — `f9ea09b5` has a `-` patch-id match |
| `wl-CG-0MU9PKH5300114KR-run-full-audit-and-produce-test-suite-re` | `9ed86341` | no | no | unrepresented | `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |
| `wl-CG-0MU9PNH4Y009BCJQ-author-reproducible-test-review-skill` | `a3ebf2c0` | no | no | unrepresented | `a3ebf2c0`, `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |
| `wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-update-project-documentation-to-referenc` | `d76ab851` | no | `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-…` | unrepresented | `d76ab851`, `a3ebf2c0`, `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |

**Correction to the original premise.** The original brief assumed all branches' work "already landed on dev via other paths". Patch-id evidence shows this is true for only **one** branch (`wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566…`). The other six each carry at least one commit with no patch-id equivalent on `dev`, and five of those six have **no `origin` counterpart** — so their commits are unrecoverable after local-ref deletion (beyond the local reflog until gc). This makes AC3 the critical safety gate.

## Desired change

- Delete the local refs proven fully represented on `dev`.
- For the remaining branches, obtain producer approval (or create a backup ref/tag) before deleting, after presenting the unrepresented commits.
- Remove now-unused worktrees that pin the branches.
- Confirm the ship Step 1 gate passes without `--skip-checks`.

## Constraints

- Never delete branches without the AC1 triage and, where required, AC3 producer approval.
- Keep the operation fully reversible where the work is not on `origin`: prefer `git tag backup/<branch> <sha>` (tags do **not** trip `git branch --no-merged`) or `refs/archive/*` over a backup *branch*, which would itself remain in the gate output.
- Do not touch `worklog/data` or other protected refs.
- Do not delete or stash unrelated worktrees; the repo has many active `wl-*` worktrees that must be preserved.
- `revert-fix` is checked out in `/tmp/wl-revert`; its worktree must be removed before the branch ref.
- `git branch -d` will refuse to delete unmerged branches; use `-D` only after AC3 approval, or delete then recreate as a backup tag.

## Key Files (predicted)

- No source files change. Relevant artefacts:
  - `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/check-unmerged-branches.js` — the gate whose output defines success.
  - `.git/refs/heads/*` — the local refs removed.
  - `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-update-project-documentation-to-referenc/` and `/tmp/wl-revert` — worktrees to remove before their branches.

## Related work

- Release that surfaced the issue: `CG-0MUDA0CLC007G6F7` (Release v0.1.17: promote dev to main).
- Ship-skill scoping gap (SorraAgents repo, not resolvable here): `SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`.
- Content WIP referenced by unrepresented commits: `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` (chain cards), `CG-0MTIILIBQ009J49F`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (high):** deleting one of the five non-origin branches discards commits with no other reachable ref. Mitigation: AC3 producer approval + backup tag/archive ref.
- **Risk (medium):** `fix-bank-hint-tutorial` and `wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566…` exist on `origin`, so local deletion is recoverable; their stale origin branches remain and may yet trip other tooling. Out of scope here; note as a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** the seven branches are herdr-workflow artefacts, not live feature work. Partially verified per AC1 (only 1 fully represented); the remainder require the AC3 handoff.
- **Scope-creep risk:** pruning the many other stale `wl-*` branches, origin branches, or worktrees is **not** in scope; capture as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (agent, intake): "For the six branches carrying commits not represented on `dev` (five with no `origin` counterpart), what is the approved disposal policy?"
  - Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer.
  - Options: (a) archive the commit SHAs/subjects in this item, then delete all seven; (b) create `backup/<branch>` **tags** (or `refs/archive/*`) for the unrepresented branches, then delete all seven; (c) delete only the fully-represented branch and keep the other six; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (b) — backup tags for the five non-origin branches are cheap and fully reversible, they do not appear in `git branch --no-merged`, and they let all seven local branches be deleted so the ship Step 1 gate passes.
  - Answer: _pending producer response_.

## Problem statement

The Tableau Card Engine ships pre-1.0 builds (currently `v0.1.17`), but nothing in the UI signals that players are using an ALPHA build. Every game screen, the game-selector menu, and the Help/Settings panes should show a brightly coloured red **ALPHA** badge carrying the current version number, so users and testers always know they are on an unreleased ALPHA build.

## Users

- **Players / testers** — "When I open any game, I can immediately see that this is an ALPHA build and which version I'm on, so I know to report issues and can quote the exact version."
- **Release manager / producer** — "I can visually confirm from any screen that the deployed build is an ALPHA build and that the running version matches the release."
- **Developers** — "The badge is rendered by one shared helper, so adding a new game scene automatically gets the ALPHA banner with no per-game work."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A bright red **ALPHA** badge displaying the current version string (from `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, i.e. the build-time `__APP_VERSION__`) is rendered **stacked above/over the title** on every Example Game scene and every Gym demo scene, delivered through the shared scene-title helper (`createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`), so no per-game bespoke code is required. The one remaining bespoke title call site — `BlackjackScene`, which draws `'Blackjack'` with its own `scene.add.text` — is migrated to `createSceneTitle()` so no bespoke title rendering remains.
2. The same red ALPHA + version badge appears stacked above/over the one-off title on the Game Selector menu screen.
3. The SettingsPanel title shows the badge stacked above/over it, and HelpPanel gains a compact **"Help" + ALPHA badge** header at the top of its content (HelpPanel currently has no title heading).
4. The badge's version text equals `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; the existing muted version labels on the menu (top-right) and settings (bottom-left) remain unchanged.
5. The badge renders correctly (legible, no clipping, no overlap with the top-left `Menu` button, the top-right HUD controls, or the existing version label) at the fixed 1280×720 design resolution used by every surface (`GAME_W` × `GAME_H`, `Phaser.Scale.FIT` with `CENTER_BOTH`); automated tests cover the shared badge helper and assert a badge showing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is created on each surface (Example Game / Gym header, Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared-helper first.** All scene/game/Gym titles already route through `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`); extend those rather than patching individual scenes. The Game Selector title, `SettingsPanel` title, and `HelpPanel` header are separate one-off call sites.
- **Reuse the version source.** Do not access `__APP_VERSION__` directly — import the existing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` / style constants from `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` so version handling stays in one place.
- **No new assets / permissive only.** Red badge must be drawn with Phaser primitives (rectangle + text); no new image assets, no new dependencies.
- **Do not remove existing version labels** (producer decision Q3a) — the badge is additive.
- **Reduced motion.** The badge is static (no animation), so it is inherently reduced-motion safe; do not add motion.
- **Canvas headroom.** Scene titles sit at `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`; a badge stacked *above* the title has little vertical room. Option (c) permits overlaying/overlapping the title's upper edge; the chosen geometry must remain legible and must not collide with the top-left `Menu` button or top-right HUD controls.
- **SLL requirement.** Positioning must respect the project's SLL/no-hardcoded-pixel rule where practical; the title helpers already own their fixed header geometry, so the badge should be defined relative to the title it decorates.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — `createSceneTitle()` (centred title at `GAME_W/2`, `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`) and `createSceneHeader()` (title + `Menu` button). Used by all Example Game renderers/scenes and `GymSceneBase.initHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` (`v<version>` from build-time `__APP_VERSION__`), `VERSION_COLOR`, `VERSION_ALPHA`, `VERSION_DEPTH`, `createVersionLabel()`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — one-off bold title `'Tableau Card Engine'` at `(GAME_W/2, 30)` with a subtitle; version label already rendered top-right below the GitHub icon.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — one-off `'Settings'` title at `(panelWidth/2, PADDING + 30)`.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — sections rendered in a scrollable content container; **no** title heading today.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — `initHeader(title)` delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.

## Desired change

Add a shared `createAlphaBadge(scene, opts)` factory (in `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` or a new `src/ui/AlphaBadge.ts`) that renders a bright red badge containing `ALPHA` and `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, positioned stacked above/over a given title (with an explicit anchor/y so callers control overlap). Wire it into `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` by default (with an opt-out flag) so every Example Game and Gym scene inherits it, then add it explicitly to the Game Selector title, the SettingsPanel title, and a new compact HelpPanel header. Keep the existing muted version labels.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Extend `tests/ui/SceneHeader.test.ts` with failing unit tests for `createAlphaBadge()`: bright red fill, `ALPHA` + `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` text, anchor/overlap geometry relative to the decorated title, and the opt-out flag.
2. Add per-surface presence tests — `tests/ui/GameSelectorScene.test.ts`, `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVersion.browser.test.ts`, and a new `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts`.
3. Implement `createAlphaBadge()` plus the default-on wiring in `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`; export the factory and constants from `src/ui/index.ts`.
4. Wire the one-off surfaces (Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header) and migrate `BlackjackScene` to `createSceneTitle()`.
5. Update documentation (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Build-Time Version Injection" section, `README.md`) and code comments.
6. Verify: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/`, then the unit profile before any push (`npm test -- --project unit` + `npm run build`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — Add `createAlphaBadge()`; render the badge from `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (default on, opt-out config).
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — Reuse `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; add red-badge style constants (or a `createAlphaBadge` export here if it fits better).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Tableau Card Engine'` title.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Settings'` title.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Add a compact `Help` + ALPHA badge header at the top of the content area.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — Export the new badge factory/constants.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — Verify the inherited header path renders the badge (likely no change if `createSceneHeader()` handles it).
- `tests/ui/*.test.ts` / `*.browser.test.ts` — Unit/integration tests for the badge helper and per-surface presence.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — add `createAlphaBadge()` and default-on wiring in `createSceneTitle()` (opt-out on `SceneTitleConfig`) / `createSceneHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — reuse `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; red badge colour and geometry constants.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — stack the badge above/over the `'Tableau Card Engine'` title.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — stack the badge above/over the `'Settings'` title.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — compact `Help` + ALPHA badge header at the top of the content area.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — export the badge factory and constants.
- `example-games/blackjack/scenes/BlackjackScene.ts` — migrate the bespoke `'Blackjack'` title to `createSceneTitle()` so it inherits the badge.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — verification only; `initHeader()` already delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.
- `tests/ui/SceneHeader.test.ts` — unit tests for `createAlphaBadge()` and the helper default behaviour.
- `tests/ui/GameSelectorScene.test.ts` — assert the badge is created on the menu title.
- `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVersion.browser.test.ts` — assert the badge renders on the settings title alongside the existing label.
- `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts` — assert the new `Help` + ALPHA badge header exists (new test file).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — update the "Build-Time Version Injection" section for the badge and helper wiring.
- `./README.md` — document the ALPHA badge on all screens.

**Note:** Paths above are the planned touch points; the `tests/ui/*.test.ts` / `*.browser.test.ts` glob in the predicted list is indicative of the coverage to add.

## Related work

- `CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W` — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed) — established the version-label pattern this item extends.
- `CG-0MSHQPDQ80015RF7` — Move the version number on the menu page below the GitHub logo (completed) — current version-label placement.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — top-of-canvas clipping.** Stacking a badge above a title at `y = 14` risks clipping at the canvas edge or colliding with the `Menu` button. *Mitigation:* define the badge geometry relative to the title with a small controlled overlap (per option (c)), and verify at supported canvas sizes; add a browser test/visual check.
- **Risk — banner overload.** Adding a badge to *all* surfaces (Q2a) could add visual noise to 30+ Gym dev scenes. *Mitigation:* keep the badge compact and consistent; it is intentional per the producer decision.
- **Risk — duplicate version indicators.** Existing muted labels plus the new badge duplicate the version on the menu/settings. *Accepted* per Q3a (badge is reinforced, not consolidated); noted as intentional.
- **Assumption —** `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is always available in scenes (it already is, via build-time `define`).
- **Assumption —** the Game Selector title has enough headroom above `y = 30` to stack a badge; if not, the badge may overlap the title's top edge (permitted by option (c)).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Temptation to restyle other HUD chrome or remove the muted version labels. Record such opportunities as linked work items, do not expand scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Context gathered before asking: all menu/game/Gym titles route through `createSceneTitle()`/`createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`), the menu title is a one-off in `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`, the settings title is in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, and `HelpPanel.ts` has no title heading. The version string already exists as build-time `__APP_VERSION__` (`src/ui/versionDisplay.ts`, currently `v0.1.17`).

- **Q1 — Visual form and placement of the ALPHA banner?**
  Options: (a) inline red pill badge to the right of each title; (b) full-width red ribbon at the canvas top; (c) red badge stacked above/over the title. Agent recommendation: (a) — keeps the title as the anchor and avoids covering HUD buttons.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (c)** — red badge stacked above/over the title.

- **Q2 — Which surfaces receive the banner?**
  Options: (a) every title (GameSelector, all example games, all Gym scenes, Help + Settings); (b) game and menu titles only; (c) menu + Help/Settings only. Agent recommendation: (a) — item says "all game screens".
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — every title, including Help and Settings headers.

- **Q3 — Help/Settings pane treatment and existing version labels?**
  Options: (a) badge on SettingsPanel title + compact "Help" + ALPHA header on HelpPanel, keep existing muted version labels; (b) SettingsPanel only; (c) remove the existing muted version labels. Agent recommendation: (a) — covers both panes while preserving existing labels.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — SettingsPanel + compact HelpPanel header; keep existing muted version labels.

Round 1 was originally raised by the `intake` skill on 2026-09-26 (comment `CG-C0MUIFEVBM006J5DY`) and flagged `needsProducerReview`; the producer answered all three questions in this session.



## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `plan` skill (auto-complete path; effort Small / risk Low, below the planning threshold): six automated review stages run against the existing content and the AC coverage review returned `proceed` (no children). Conservative corrections applied:
  - AC1: made the "shared helper covers every title" claim accurate — `BlackjackScene` still draws its own title with `scene.add.text` and is now explicitly in scope for migration to `createSceneTitle()` (verified by source inspection).
  - AC5: replaced the vague "supported Game Selector canvas sizes" with the project's actual fixed 1280×720 design resolution (`GAME_W`/`GAME_H`, `Phaser.Scale.FIT`) and named the four surfaces that must be asserted.
  - Added a test-first **Implementation order** section.
  - Added a canonical `**Key Files:**` block (added `BlackjackScene`, `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`; validated path syntax).
- No new child work items were created: the item is a single, small, end-to-end slice (one shared helper + four call sites + tests + docs).
- Appendix questions Q1–Q3 were already answered by the producer during intake; no new questions were raised by this planning pass.

### Appendix revision note

- Round 1 (Q1–Q3) recorded verbatim above; answers unchanged. The only addition is the AC1 clarification for `BlackjackScene`, which is a factual correction (the scene does not use `createSceneTitle()` today) and does not alter the producer's Q2a decision that every title carries the badge.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/golf/replay.test.ts Replay CLI -- transcript validation
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
AssertionError: expected Error: Could not auto-detect game type (fixture not found at ../../example-games/golf/tests/fixtures/transcripts/fixture-game.json) to contain version
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout `dev` (the failure is reproducible at `a341ec3c`).
2. Run the failing test with **no** `GAMES_CONFIG` override (the documented default unit profile):
   `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts`
   (equivalent: `/skill:test --type unit`)
3. Observe 4 failures in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (12 passed, 5 skipped):
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for wrong transcript version`
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for missing initialState`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should reject v1 transcript when --stop-at is used`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should accept v1 transcript for regular replay (no --stop-at)`
4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Root Cause & Reproduction

`scripts/replay.ts` is core-owned and registers replay adapters from the **active build preset** via `registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())`. The default preset is `core-only` (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` → `DEFAULT_PRESET`), which registers **no** adapters. Adapter auto-detection then fails with `Could not auto-detect game type from transcript. Available adapters: none.` (and `--game golf` fails with `Unknown game type 'golf'. Available adapters: none`).

`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }`, so it inherits whatever `GAMES_CONFIG` the runner provides:

- **Red:** a bare `npx vitest run --project unit …` and the project-local `/skill:test --type unit` profile (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) do **not** export `GAMES_CONFIG`, so the preset is `core-only` and the 4 tests above fail.
- **Green:** `npm test`, `npm run test:smoke` and `npm run test:dev` set `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` in their shell runners, so the golf adapter is registered and the tests pass.

A separate **latent** defect was already fixed on `dev` while this plan ran: `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` was `'../../example-games/golf/…'`, resolving one level above the repo root (introduced when the test moved to `tests/golf/` in `fbee2e51`). Corrected to `'example-games/golf/…'` in `a341ec3c`. That fix is necessary but **not sufficient** — under `core-only` the test still fails.

## Chosen Fix (producer-confirmed 2026-09-26)

**Option 1 — test-local, keep the test hermetic.** Export the preset the test needs to the spawned CLI, e.g. in `runReplay()`:

```ts
env: { ...process.env, GAMES_CONFIG: process.env.GAMES_CONFIG ?? 'full' },
```

Rationale: `/skill:test --type unit` is the documented "minimum bar for every change" and `npx vitest run --project unit tests/<game>/` is the documented targeted command, so this file must pass with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset. Forcing `full` only as a fallback preserves an explicitly supplied preset and keeps the core unit profiles runnable under `core-only` — consistent with `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` ("core test profiles must stay runnable even with a bad `GAMES_CONFIG`").

**Rejected (Option 2):** adding `GAMES_CONFIG=full` to the `unit`/`smoke`/`dev` commands in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`. This is agent infrastructure out of bounds for agents and would not fix a bare `npx vitest run` for a developer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` passes under the **default unit profile with no `GAMES_CONFIG` override** — `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (and `/skill:test --type unit`) reports 0 failures — while continuing to pass under `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (`npm test`).
2. The test documents (in a code comment) why it pins `GAMES_CONFIG` to the full preset, and the already-corrected `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path (`example-games/golf/…`) is preserved. Related documentation is updated if any workflow/profile behaviour changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

**Key Files:**

- `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` — set the `GAMES_CONFIG` fallback in the spawned CLI env; document the preset dependency; keep the corrected fixture path.
- `scripts/replay.ts` — context only: preset-driven adapter registration (`registerConfiguredAdapters`); no change expected.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — context only: `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'`; no change expected.

**Classification: transient CPU-contention worker RPC timeout that Vitest surfaced as a failed file/test, which disables the existing retry mitigation and therefore fails the gate.**

Supporting evidence, all reproducible from this checkout:

1. **The retry mitigation never fired.** `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` emits
   `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed args="--project unit"` in
   the recorded output — a single attempt. `runWithRetry` only retries when
   `shouldRetryOnce(output)` is true, and that masking guard requires an
   **all-files-passed** summary
   (`/Test Files\s+\d+\s+passed \(\d+\)/` plus no `failed` counts). This run
   reported `Test Files 1 failed | 416 passed (417)` and `Tests 1 failed`, so the
   guard returns false and the stage exits 1 without retrying.
2. **The guard gap is confirmed by direct predicate evaluation.** The runner's
   captured output is preserved at
   `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt`. Evaluating the
   exported predicate against it:
   `shouldRetryOnce(<actual recorded output>) === false`, while the *same*
   output with only the two summary counts edited to the all-passed form
   (`Test Files 416 passed (416)` / `Tests 7164 passed | 8 skipped (7172)`)
   returns `true`. The sole difference between recovery and gate failure is
   Vitest counting the poisoned file as failed.
3. **The failure is not reproducible at either failing commit.**
   - **Same-commit proof (strongest):** occurrence 2 was on `933644bc` with a
     **418-file** corpus (`Test Files 1 failed | 417 passed (418)`,
     `Tests 1 failed | 7172 passed | 8 skipped (7181)`). Re-running the unit
     stage at that *same* commit ~60 minutes later produced
     `Test Files 418 passed (418)`,
     `Tests 7173 passed | 8 skipped (7181)`,
     `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=0 outcome=clean args="--project unit"`.
     Identical commit, identical 418-file/7181-test corpus, one red run and one
     green run — the failure is non-deterministic, not a defect in the code
     under test.
   - **Corroborating proof:** `git show --name-status` confirms the only test
     changes since occurrence 1 (`a341ec3c`) are **additions**
     (`tests/main-street/pawn-shop-reputation.test.ts`, +8 unit tests) and one
     browser-test edit — no pre-existing unit test file was modified. Every unit
     test present at `a341ec3c` therefore also ran and passed at HEAD.
4. **Contention context.** Both poisoned attempts recorded collect ≈370s and
   tests ≈630-665s, against `collect 211.71s, tests 349.42s` on the clean
   re-run — roughly 1.8-1.9× — consistent with concurrent suites competing for
   CPU on the same host. This is the documented transient class from
   CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE and CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N.

| Run | Commit | Outcome | Test Files | Tests | collect/tests | `[vitest-runner]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (incident) | `a341ec3c` | red | 1 failed \| 416 passed (417) | 1 failed \| 7164 passed \| 8 skipped | 371.18s / 665.35s | `attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed` |
| 2 (incident) | `933644bc` | red | 1 failed \| 417 passed (418) | 1 failed \| 7172 passed \| 8 skipped | 369.62s / 631.88s | `attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed` |
| 3 (re-run) | `933644bc` | **green** | 418 passed (418) | 7173 passed \| 8 skipped | 211.71s / 349.42s | `attempts=1 status=0 outcome=clean` |

**Discriminator resolved for the sibling item:** CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU (the same
signature, previously mitigated) recorded that it could not tell whether the
poisoned run was the only attempt or the retry. Both occurrences here report
`attempts=1`, which answers that: on these recurrences the run was the **only**
attempt, because the transient presented with a failed-file summary and
therefore never qualified for a retry. The previous mitigation covers the
*all-passed* variant of the transient; these recurrences expose the
*failed-file* variant, which the masking guard cannot distinguish from a genuine
failure. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`'s `tail -20` also means the console log names
neither the failed file nor a distinct assertion, so the failure is only
diagnosable from the runner's summary line — see the evidence gap below.

### Evidence gap (closed by the approved scope)

`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` pipes each stage through `tail -20`, so the persisted
output does not name the failing test/file and does not show whether Vitest
reported a distinct assertion error alongside the worker-timeout unhandled
error. We therefore could not tell whether the counted failure was *purely* the
`onTaskUpdate` timeout artefact or a real test that also exceeded its own
timeout under the same contention. **Producer decision (2026-09-26): remove the
truncation** so the next recurrence is fully diagnosable — see AC7.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout a341ec3c2d92bca48035e7d09ca1fec24da726c0`
2. Run the failing stage: `npm --silent test` (Vitest via `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`; there is no pytest suite in this repository).
   To reproduce the unit stage alone: `npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit`
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item — in particular the `[vitest-runner]` summary line (attempts/outcome) and the identity of any failed test file, neither of which survives the `tail -20` truncation in the excerpt above.

## Impact

The unit stage of the full suite exits 1 although every test passes on re-run,
so the release/push gate fails spuriously and must be retried manually. This is
the second recurrence of this transient class (after CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU) and it
blocks PR creation for the agent's current work item whenever it fires. It is
currently live: occurrence 2 was observed on `dev` HEAD `933644bc` at
18:08:03Z, and the same commit's re-run was green — so the gate can fail at any
time under host CPU contention, with no code change involved.

**Note:** triage also surfaced a *distinct* latent defect while investigating —
`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` is not self-contained and fails under a bare
`npx vitest run --project unit` (it needs `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, which only
`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` exports). It is **not** this failure (it would report
4 failed tests, not 1) and has been filed separately as
**CG-0MUIRPUX9003T24V**, discovered-from this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Root cause closed, not bypassed (approach (a), producer-confirmed 2026-09-26):** the retry mitigation recovers from a worker RPC timeout that Vitest reports *as a failed file*, while still refusing to retry or accept a genuine per-file assertion failure that merely coincides with the transient signature. The mitigation attributes the reported failures: only when every reported failure is the worker-timeout signature itself may the run be treated as transient (retry once; accept if the retry is again purely transient). *Verified by:* extended unit tests in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` covering (a) a transient signature with a failed-file summary attributable only to the timeout — which must be retried/accepted — and (b) a genuine assertion failure alongside the signature — which must still be refused. The existing conservative cases in that file must remain passing.
- **The recorded failing run becomes a regression fixture:** the predicate is exercised against the real captured output of this incident (or an equivalent verbatim excerpt) so the recurrence cannot silently return. *Verified by:* a test in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` that asserts the incident-shaped output is treated as transient while a genuine failure bearing the same signature is not.
- **Failure classification recorded with evidence:** the transient signature is confirmed non-reproducible via a green re-run whose `[vitest-runner]` line shows `status=0`, and the mechanism that defeated the retry is demonstrated from the recorded output. *Status: met by this planning session* — see *Failure Classification* above.
- **Gate verified green:** `npm --silent test` (or, at minimum, its unit stage) exits 0 at `dev` HEAD — and, because this is a non-deterministic contention flake, the AC is satisfied by demonstrating a green stage together with the mitigation's recovery path rather than by a single green run. *Verified by:* the `[vitest-runner]` summary line (`status=0`, plus any `retry-clean`/`accepted-transient` outcome under contention) together with a run in which a synthetic transient-with-failed-file input is recovered.
- **CI stage output is no longer truncated (producer-confirmed 2026-09-26):** no stage of `npm test` in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` pipes its output through `tail -20` (or, if bounded, persists the full untruncated output), so a recurrence names the failed test/file and shows any distinct assertion error alongside the transient signature. Stale comments referencing the truncation (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` module docstring, `scripts/run-electron-smoke.sh`, `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` section comment) are updated or removed.
- **Shared truncation pattern reconciled:** the same `tail -20` pattern in `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` and `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` is either aligned with the CI runner or explicitly recorded as a follow-up work item. *Verified by:* the diff or the recorded follow-up id.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the change, including the CPU-contention mitigation section of `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, the retry-guard rationale in `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`'s module docstring, and the quality-gate wording in `AGENTS.md` if the accepted-run semantics change.
- **Full project test suite passes with the new changes.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — `shouldRetryOnce()` masking guard and `runWithRetry()`; the site of the gap.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — guard predicate coverage; must be extended with the incident-shaped case (and its truncation section comment updated).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — stage wiring, `--timeout-ms` bounds, and the `tail -20` truncation to remove (AC7).
- `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` — the same `tail -20` pattern (AC8: align or record a follow-up).
- `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` — the same `tail -20` pattern (AC8: align or record a follow-up).
- `scripts/run-electron-smoke.sh` — comment explaining its summary line survives the CI wrapper's truncation; stale once AC7 lands.
- `vite.config.ts` — `unit` project `maxWorkers: 4` CPU-contention cap.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — CPU-contention mitigation and test-profile documentation.
- `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt` — the recorded failing-run output used as evidence/fixture source.

## Proposed approach

**Decision (producer, 2026-09-26):** approach **(a) attribution-aware retry**,
plus removing the CI stage truncation. Approach (b) is **rejected**.

- **(a) Attribution-aware retry — CONFIRMED.** When the transient signature is
  present *and* the summary reports failures, attribute the failures: if every
  reported failure is the worker-timeout signature itself (no distinct
  assertion/original error), treat the run as transient — retry once, and accept
  if the retry is again purely transient. A distinct assertion failure keeps the
  guard refusing, exactly as today. This requires the runner to inspect the
  failure section rather than only the summary counts. This preserves the
  documented "never mask a genuine failure" guarantee.
- **(b) Unconditional retry-once on the signature — REJECTED.** Retrying
  whenever the signature appears (using the last attempt's result) would let a
  genuinely flaky failure pass on retry, weakening the documented masking
  guarantee and the deliberate test at
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts:87` ("returns false when the
  timeout signature is present alongside genuine file failures").

**Confirmed hardening (AC7):** `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` no longer pipes stage
output through `tail -20`, so a future recurrence names the poisoned file and
shows whether a distinct assertion accompanied the timeout. Removing the
truncation also makes the runner's end-of-output `[vitest-runner]` summary line
non-load-bearing, so the comments that explain their survival purpose must be
updated rather than left stale.

**Order (test-first):** extend `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` with
the incident-shaped case and confirm it fails against the current predicate,
then change the predicate — per the project's test-first discipline. The change
must be small enough to read as one function's contract, not a rewrite of the
runner.

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

- Contention mitigation background: CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE, CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N
- Discovered item: CG-0MUIRPUX9003T24V (golf replay test hermeticity)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Research findings (no producer interview was required for this item)

- **Q: Is the reported failure reproducible at the failing commit?**
  **Answer (research, this session): No — proven at the same commit.** The unit
  stage was re-run green at `dev` HEAD `933644bc` (`Test Files 418 passed (418)`,
  `Tests 7173 passed | 8 skipped`, `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=0
  outcome=clean`) while incident occurrence 2 on the *same* commit reported
  `Test Files 1 failed | 417 passed (418)` and `Tests 1 failed | 7172 passed |
  8 skipped` — the same 418-file / 7181-test corpus, red then green. The commits
  since occurrence 1 only *added* tests
  (`tests/main-street/pawn-shop-reputation.test.ts`, +8 unit tests) and edited a
  browser test; `git show --name-status` confirms no pre-existing unit test file
  was modified, so every unit test at `a341ec3c` also ran and passed at HEAD.
- **Q: Why did the retry mitigation not recover either run?**
  **Answer (research, this session): because `shouldRetryOnce()` requires an
  all-files-passed summary.** Evaluated against the recorded occurrence-1 output
  it returns `false`; evaluated against the same output with only the summary
  counts edited to the all-passed form it returns `true`. Both occurrences
  report `attempts=1`, confirming no retry was attempted. Evidence:
  `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt`, the triage-bot
  comment recording occurrence 2, and `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`.
- **Q: Is `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (which fails locally) the reported failure?**

# Task: Decide the repo publication mechanism and add its test contract

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I have a fixed, tested contract for how the nine
`tce-*` GitHub repositories are created and which refs they carry, so that the
publication step (C2/C4) is reproducible, idempotent and safe.

## Context

Split from **CG-0MUHK5NND0024J1S** (*Create the nine tce-* GitHub repositories
and push extracted history*), which was itself split out of F4
(CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK). The producer decisions are already recorded in the parent
Appendix: **public** repos (Q1), `dev` → `main` with `main` seeded once (Q2),
extract from the current `dev` HEAD and record the SHA (Q3), publish only
`dev` + `main` — no monorepo feature/`wl-*` branches and no `v0.1.x` tags (Q4).
What is **not** yet fixed is *how* the create-and-push step is driven, and that
is what this task decides and pins down with tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A decision record exists (new `docs/dev/repo-publication-decision.md`, or a
   new sub-section of `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`) that fixes all of:
   (a) script-driven publication vs documented manual commands; (b) the exact
   creation command (`gh repo create --public` with `--source`/`--push` or a
   separate `git push`); (c) the ref contract (`dev` plus `main` seeded from
   `dev`, `main` as default, nothing else); (d) idempotency (an existing repo is
   never re-created, and a re-run is a no-op when the refs are up to date);
   (e) safety guards (never rewrite or force-push the source monorepo; never
   push the launcher repo's `main`; abort on an unexpected repo-name collision
   rather than overwriting).
2. A new `tests/scripts/repo-publication.test.ts` encodes that contract as
   executable unit tests (`--project unit`): target/remote resolution from
   `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (nine repos), `--public` visibility, the
   exact pushed ref set, idempotent re-run behaviour, and each safety guard.
   The tests describe the helper interface that C2 implements. Because the
   helper does not exist yet, the behavioural cases are authored as documented
   `it.skip(...)` contracts (so the suite stays green); C2 unskips and satisfies
   them.
3. The decision record lists the exact fresh-clone verification commands that
   C5 executes for the parent's AC3/AC4.
4. A concise decision summary is recorded as a comment on the parent
   CG-0MUHK5NND0024J1S.

## Minimal Implementation

- Read `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (single source of truth),
  `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (the existing extraction/target-name convention:
  `core` for the core repo, game names for games) and §5 of
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- Write the decision record for the publication contract only — extraction,
  rename and scaffolding are already decided and out of scope here.
- Author the test file against the chosen helper interface; keep it free of
  tautologies (it must fail if the helper ignores a guard).
- No behaviour change to extraction, scaffolding or the launcher.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/repo-publication-decision.md` — new decision record (or a new
  sub-section of `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`).
- `tests/scripts/repo-publication.test.ts` — new contract tests.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — read-only source of truth for
  names/remotes.

**Dependencies:**

None. The producer decisions required to fix the contract are already recorded
in the parent's Appendix (Q1–Q4).

**Deliverables:**

- Publication decision record.
- Test file defining the publication contract.

`git cherry`/patch-id cannot drop an intermediate commit from a branch without rewriting it; the deletable unit is the **branch ref**.

### Expanded: exactly what the unique / absent changes are

**1. `8ffdae34` — banking-hint tutorial fix (functional; highest value)**
- File: `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` (logic now lives on `dev` at `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`).
- Diff: `if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)` → `if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)`.
- Effect: the one-shot banking hint fires only **after** the tutorial is complete; previously it fired mid-tutorial when the player had spare actions, creating a dead end and a stale tutorial step.
- Status on `dev`: **bug still present** — `MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts:118` retains the `tut?.isActive` (non-negated) condition and the comment "when the tutorial is active …".

**2. `8c3d12f1` — left-align end-turn coin grid (functional)**
- Files: `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts`, `scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts`, `example-games/main-street/README.md`, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts`, `coin-grid.browser.test.ts`, `coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts`.
- Diff: `packCoins` moves from centre-anchored to left-anchored packing — `x: col*(w+s) - finalGridW/2 + w/2` → `x: col*(w+s) + w/2`, drops `finalGridW`, adds `COIN_GRID_LEFT_INSET = 8`; default `availableWidth` `cardW/2` → `cardW - 2*inset`; default anchor `cardW/4` → `-cardW/2 + inset`.
- Effect: the coin grid reads left→right from the card's left inset and never re-centres as coins are added (previously bottom-right quadrant, re-centred).
- Status on `dev`: **absent** — `dev`'s `coin-grid.ts` still uses `- finalGridW / 2` and the bottom-right default.

**3. `9e792ac3` — transcript week/year stamping + calendar tests (feature)**
- Files: `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts`, new `tests/main-street/CalendarSaveLoad.test.ts` (99 lines).
- Diff: `MainStreetTranscriptEvent` gains `& { week?: number; year?: number }`; new `MainStreetCalendarStamp`; `MainStreetTranscriptRecorder.deriveCalendar(turn)` computes week/year from the recorder's initial calendar + turn offset (52→1 wrap, year increment); `recordEvent()` stamps every event; `MainStreetLifecycleManager` snapshots `week`/`year` into the recorder initial snapshot (attach + seed re-init).
- Tests: serialize/deserialize round-trip; legacy-save migration defaults; transcript stamping; 52→1 wrap; legacy-snapshot default.
- Status on `dev`: **absent** — `dev`'s `MainStreetTranscript.ts` has no week/year stamping (the calendar exists only in serialized state, `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`).

**4. `9ed86341` — `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` (doc; 840 lines / ~7,850 words)**
- New file only. Value audit of the then-501-file test suite: inventory + decision totals; methodology + six anti-pattern categories + discovery probes; scan results; 2 removal recommendations (R1 `MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, 721 lines; R2 `dev-server-cleanup.test.ts`, 222 lines); 9 clean-up recommendations; watch-list; tracking; blockers; Appendix A (full 501-file classification table); Appendix B (reproduction steps).
- Status on `dev`: **absent**.

**5. `a3ebf2c0` — `.pi/skills/test-review` skill (tooling)**
- Files: `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` (223 lines), `.pi/skills/test-review/scripts/scan-self-referential.sh` (36 lines).
- Content: reproducible procedure for the TCE test-suite value audit (anti-patterns: source-code-grep, placeholder/tautological, self-referential simulations, duplicates, type-level/structural-only, zero-assertion browser tests); classification procedure, report format, child-work-item convention, re-run/diff procedure, self-test. The script lists test files importing zero production code (whitespace-tolerant).
- Status on `dev`: **absent**.

**6. `f426ffd7` — competitive-mode doc/comment additions (doc/comment only; low value)**
- Files: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` (+~16 lines), `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` (+11-line header comment), `MainStreetState.ts` (+7-line module comment). Adds a "Status update (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30)" note marking competitive mode a deliberate superseded scope extension and documents the competitive state model/harness.
- Status on `dev`: **absent** (exact text), but the competitive feature itself is on `dev`; preserving it is optional.

### Question for the producer (mechanics)

Given the entanglement, how should the discard decisions be applied?

- **(A) Salvage then delete** — create a fresh branch from `dev`, cherry-pick the preserve commits you want (`8ffdae34`, `8c3d12f1`, `9e792ac3`, optionally `9ed86341`/`a3ebf2c0`/`f426ffd7`), land them via `/skill:implement`, then delete all 7 local branches.
- **(B) Backup-tag then delete** — `git tag backup/<branch> <sha>` for the branches carrying preserve commits, then delete all 7 local branches (unique work recoverable from tags). Recommended as the minimal step to unblock the ship gate now.
- **(C) Delete `wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566` only** — the sole discard-only branch; leave the other 6 until salvage is decided.
- **(D) Delete all 7 with no preservation** — explicitly discards the unique/absent work (not recommended; AC3).

**Recommended: (B)**, followed by a separate salvage work item for the two functional fixes (`8ffdae34`, `8c3d12f1`) and the transcript week/year feature (`9e792ac3`).
